description: The first family-F26 arm (DECISIONS.md 9.144, 9.145): the F25 run stack on a demand where every declared ride driver owns a car. The escort binder and the 9.60 lift pass tested a LICENCE alone where the joint and shared passes also required a household vehicle, so 6,165 WEEKDAY escort bindings (5,426 drivers) and 3,154 lift bindings (2,697 drivers) named a driver with no car, and the seed then put 85,993 non-car legs on trips those same persons' own `boundDriveTrips` declared them to drive - now 0, with `serve_tours_carless` 0 on all three day types. Bindings 375,007 -> 375,307 and the seeded ride share 0.0444 -> 0.0448, because the occupancy identity re-lets the freed volume to drivers who can actually drive. What the arm must answer, in order. (1) THE PAIRING LOSS, and it is now a sharp question rather than a diffuse one. 9.145 establishes on the code that a declared pair faces NO clock test (`if (!isDeclared && gap > window)`, since 9.120), so a declared pair can never be recorded as a window miss: `miss_window` means the DECLARED DRIVER WAS ABSENT and a substitute was found at the wrong hour. At the F25 gate the four buckets summed exactly to the 16,778 unpaired legs and 14,766 of them - 88% - were that one class. A declared driver can leave `car` only by SELECTING a seeded plan that never held it, since `GatedSubtourModeChoice` gates proposals and not memories, and this family's rebuild removed exactly those plans. The new `miss_declared_absent` column in `output/ride_pairing.csv` names the class directly: if it falls to near zero, 9.144 closed the route and the pair rate should recover from F25's 0.7827; if it does not, the next root is the intra-household SCOPE of `EscortCoherenceListener`, which leaves the lift and shared passes - 170,582 of 375,307 WEEKDAY bindings, 45.4% - with nothing that re-proposes either half of a drifted pair. (2) RIDE ITSELF. It read -43.1% at the F25 gate against a seeded share that had risen 31% without moving the realised one, which falsified the whole demand-side class of explanation. Roughly 3 pp of the 8.9 pp gap was attributed to execution and ~6 pp to ride not being SELECTED at all; a pairing recovery should move the first and leave the second, which is what separates the two halves of the lane. (3) CAR, BIKE and TAXI. An unpaired ride leg executes as a drive where the passenger can drive and a walk where they cannot, so ride's deficit is partly worn by car (+11.4%), bike (+122.6%) and taxi (+145.1%); a real pairing gain should draw those down together, and if ride rises while nothing falls, the accounting is not what it looks like. (4) The pt SPLIT is a CONTROL: heavy rail +242.6% and bus +37.6% against light rail -56.4%. Nothing in this family touches pt, so it should read roughly as F25 did, and a large move means the demand rebuild reached further than intended. (5) CONVERGENCE, GOAL.md requirement 8, still unmeasured: innovation switches off at 240 and the post-cutoff window straddles 250, so this arm can measure it if it survives its gates. (6) The awaiting-run measurements the open issues name: #86, #48, #93, #96, #94, #98, #108, #107, #82, #131, #30, #49, #50, #66. S2 x WEEKDAY at 25%, 300 iterations, innovation off at 240, gated every 100 iterations under the loop in GOAL.md with the runner's own watcher stopping the hard bar itself (9.137) - in which case the arm closes itself out as `stopped_at_gate` and its reading is citable at its `reached_iteration` and nowhere past it (9.143). 25% is the standing directive (user, 1 Sep). Cost: MEASURED, not projected - the F25 arm settled at a median 306 s an iteration and reached iteration 100 in 33,535 s, so 300 iterations is ~26 h. Graph rendering is OFF (9.59). THE COMPILED CONTROLER DIFFERS FROM F25's by one appended diagnostic column and the counter behind it (9.145): it consumes no randomness, alters no branch condition, mode, score or draw, and is behaviour-neutral by construction, so F26 remains ONE family across it - but nothing before the F26 boundary compares with anything after it, the demand having been rebuilt (9.127, 9.138, 9.142, 9.143, 9.144). NOTHING THIS PRODUCES IS A RESULT until its record says `ran_to_last_iteration`.
